guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
An external guru who demands surrender places themselves where the source should be. But surrender does not always look like pressure. Sometimes it happens from our side. Praise, mirroring, pity, attraction, special attention, or the feeling of being deeply seen can make the child hand over judgment voluntarily.
brief:
- the main point: an outside guru who demands surrender puts themselves where the source should be, the opposite of the inner Guide, which points beyond itself (P8); and surrender can come from our side, when mirroring, special attention or the feeling of being deeply seen make your little one hand over its judgment willingly.
- what the dedup leaves to add (experiments/t56-guide/DEDUP-REPORT.md, group 10): the guru standing where the source should be (G10.1); mirroring and special attention as ways judgment gets handed over (G10.3, small).
- already in the article, so not said again as new: without an inner Guide it's easy to go looking for one in a cult (The Chicken-and-Egg Problem); somebody who seems grown-up can feel like salvation, leaning on them can help for a while, a teacher should "wean us from dependency altogether", "Borrow adulthood. Do not surrender it." (Don't Give the Inner Adult Away); praise or pity, fear or attraction, or something that really resonates with you making what you knew slip away (Untangling the Belonging Bargains, a few paragraphs before this h1).
- stance (STANCE-LEDGER.md): keep the scope, a guru who demands surrender, not every teacher; leaning on someone "can actually help for a while".
- left for the next groups: private attention or specialness making contrary evidence disappear (group 12, love bombing); manipulators who present as flawed but honest (group 11).
